findings.impact: A malicious or unexpected commit can disclose or modify local data, and untracked external inputs can make a conservative report unsound.
findings.text: The commit-only design permits materializing Git tree entries while preserving modes but does not constrain symlink dereferencing or filesystem containment. A committed source symlink to an absolute or parent-relative path can make a naive analyzer read outside the claimed snapshot (including private local files) or let materialization/write/cleanup escape the temporary root; external target bytes also are not covered by the snapshot identity. Require safe no-follow or proven contained, explicitly pinned resolution and unbounded gaps when link dependencies cannot be modeled; protect writes and cleanup, and test absolute/relative/link-chain escapes against external sentinels.

output.summary: Committed-snapshot symlink containment is specified and the prior finding is resolved.
Approved portable commit-only analysis and committed symlink handling.

responses.adversary_design:5:1: fixed: Define no-follow or same-tree proven link resolution, unbounded fallback for unsupported or escaping dependencies, root-contained creation and cleanup, and sentinel tests for absolute, relative and chained escapes.

output.summary: Require safe handling of committed symlinks and root-contained materialization, with conservative gaps where link dependencies cannot be proven inside the pinned tree. Add escape, link-chain and cleanup tests without changing the portable commit-only scope.
Both reviews approve the committed-snapshot symlink and containment boundaries; the prior finding is resolved. No open findings or notes require verdicts.

Implementation review requests changes on four material findings: replacement-ref identity, unconditional full fallback, packaged grammar/cache identity, and missing regression tests. These reopen implementation and test design. No non-material notes require verdicts.

responses.review_impl:1:1: fixed: Every analyzer Git subprocess uses --no-replace-objects; commit, tree and blob replacement-ref contract tests pass.
responses.review_impl:1:2: disputed: Identical populated Git trees now analyze inputs and return complete when no actual gaps exist. Changed trees still require unbounded fallback because callbacks, resources, dynamic dispatch and cross-file resolution remain unmodeled; treating those relationships as complete would violate the approved design. No unsupported scope is claimed.
responses.review_impl:1:3: fixed: Grammar identity hashes the actual depth and breadth grammars, queries and runtimes, including missing-asset markers, and keys extraction caches with that identity. The real offline npm tarball test confirms identity and warm cache reuse without package-lock.

output.summary: Pin Git object reads against replacement refs, compute grammar and cache identity from shipped grammar and runtime bytes, and support valid unchanged populated comparisons while reusing compatible extraction facts. Changed comparisons remain conservatively full-fallback until dependency completeness can be proven.

not: A new graph service, a replacement test runner or a separately implemented multilingual parser.
Predict which tests will fail, promise the mathematically smallest selection, or infer external integration state from Git alone.
principles: Test selection and execution require no model reasoning during normal runs.
intent.purpose: Determine which tests to run based on a git changeset.
intent.serves: Developers, CI, and agents performing repeated unit and integration test runs during development.

output.summary: Symlink and materialization boundaries preserve pinned-tree identity and containment.

findings.impact: The report can validate and cache analysis of a different source tree than the exact commit requested.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts Git commands honor replace refs: a requested commit ID can be paired with a different commit’s tree and replacement blob bytes. Disable replacement effects or verify real objects for every endpoint/tree/blob read.

findings.impact: The analyzer cannot enable sparse execution for any normal repository, even with identical endpoints and a compatible passing baseline.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts unconditionally emits an unbounded gap for every changed tree and every identical nonempty tree. Implement justified supported completeness or bounded scopes, including a valid unchanged populated tree, rather than always forcing full-profile fallback.

findings.impact: Normal installations report an indistinguishable unavailable grammar identity and always disable extraction caching, undermining reproducibility and repeated-run performance.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts derives grammar identity and the raw extraction cache key from package-lock.json, but package.json excludes this file from the npm distribution. Use shipped actual grammar identities and enable safe extraction cache reuse in installed packages.

findings.impact: The current test suite passes while exact identity can be falsified and sparse execution and production cache reuse never occur.
findings.text: test/conservative-impact-contract.test.ts checks valid empty only for empty repositories and lacks replacement-ref and actual packed-install checks. Add regression coverage for immutable commit/tree/blob IDs under Git replacements, unchanged populated trees without fabricated full fallback, and installed package grammar identity/cache reuse.

output.summary: Exact Git identity, universally forced fallback, and packaged grammar/cache behavior require correction.

findings.text: The packed-package test builds from git archive HEAD rather than the current checkout. Running npm test after an uncommitted implementation or package metadata edit can test an old distribution, hiding new regressions or falsely reporting a fixed defect. Materialize a safe isolated copy of the actual current test source (including relevant modified and added inputs), while retaining offline dependencies and protecting concurrent tests from shared build outputs.

output.summary: Isolated source copy now includes current checkout edits and additions; remaining finding resolved.

spec: Implement conservative impact analysis directly in this Trail-code fork specified in docs/test-impact/design.md, sections 1–6, 8, 11–13 and delivery steps 1–2. Use upstream base ca20a67764e99531a1cf272eea8354e2c16f71d9 and define versioned impact contracts and exact explicit endpoints. Analyze both snapshots, preserve ambiguity and analysis gaps, traverse complete reverse dependencies without arbitrary limits, handle deletions, renames and rebinding, and isolate and validate conservative caches. Report justified fallback scopes instead of silently omitting uncertainty. Include meaningful tests for endpoint semantics, graph completeness, gaps, cache freshness and representative dependency cases. Preserve upstream licensing and document the pinned source. Do not implement a replacement parser or assume normal navigation output is conservative. The full design and its acceptance matrix are binding; resolve open distribution and interface choices through the workflow. Work directly in this fork for a future upstream pull request; no separate test-impact repository or Git subtree. Preserve the separate Unity plugin branch. Where the design refers to a separate fork and adapter distribution, adapt it to this unified repository. Owner scope clarification: Initial release requires explicit committed Git endpoints only, and must work across platforms and filesystems with ordinary Git repositories, without Btrfs, privileged operations, special mounts or subvolumes. Worktree target support is deferred; reject it clearly rather than silently substituting a commit. Preserve exact target execution identity and protection against mutations, and adapt the original worktree-specific acceptance cases accordingly.
title: Build conservative two-snapshot impact analysis
